en: When I was a kid, I played in the street every afternoon.
es: Cuando era niño, jugaba en la calle todas las tardes.
why: Every afternoon is a habit.

en: It was raining when we left.
es: Llovía cuando salimos.
why: Rain is the background scene.

en: Tomás opened the door and saw a parrot.
es: Tomás abrió la puerta y vio un loro.
why: One action after another.

en: Last night Vale called me twice.
es: Anoche Vale me llamó dos veces.
why: Two calls is a counted event.

en: Vale was tired, so she went to bed early.
es: Vale estaba cansada, así que se acostó temprano.
why: Tired is the state behind the action.

en: Vale was at the hospital for three days.
es: Vale estuvo tres días en el hospital.
why: Three days is a closed stretch.

en: We lived in Medellín for five years, and then we moved.
es: Vivimos cinco años en Medellín y luego nos mudamos.
why: Five years then a move, a closed period.

en: At six the bus arrived and everyone got on.
es: A las seis llegó el bus y todos subieron.
why: One event in the story.

en: The bus arrived at six every day.
es: El bus llegaba a las seis todos los días.
why: Every day is a habit.

en: When I was little, my grandmother made arepas every Sunday.
es: Cuando yo era chiquito, mi abuela hacía arepas todos los domingos.
why: Every Sunday means a habit, not one event.

en: Yesterday Tomás made the coffee for the whole café.
es: Ayer Tomás hizo el café para todo el local.
why: One finished job yesterday.

en: Don Hernando used to go to the plaza every afternoon.
es: Don Hernando iba a la plaza todas las tardes.
why: Every afternoon is a repeated habit.

en: Last Saturday Vale went to Villa de Leyva.
es: El sábado pasado Vale fue a Villa de Leyva.
why: One trip, finished.

en: Rosa had a lot of work, so she stayed until ten.
es: Rosa tenía mucho trabajo, así que se quedó hasta las diez.
why: Staying until ten is one finished event.

en: When we were kids, we always had lunch at my aunt's house.
es: Cuando éramos niños, siempre almorzábamos en la casa de mi tía.
why: Always means a habit.

en: Tomás came in, saw Vale and said hello.
es: Tomás entró, vio a Vale y la saludó.
why: A chain of finished events, one after another.

en: The café was small and it smelled like fresh bread.
es: El café era pequeño y olía a pan fresco.
why: This describes how the place was.

en: The party was amazing, and everyone danced until two.
es: La fiesta fue increíble y todos bailaron hasta las dos.
why: Judging the whole party as one finished thing.

en: Rosa was cleaning the tables when the phone rang.
es: Rosa limpiaba las mesas cuando sonó el teléfono.
why: The cleaning was in progress when the phone rang.

en: The phone rang and Rosa answered right away.
es: Sonó el teléfono y Rosa contestó enseguida.
why: Answering is a new event after the ring.

en: Back then Vale worked at a bakery and lived near the river.
es: En esa época Vale trabajaba en una panadería y vivía cerca del río.
why: Back then sets a period as background.

en: Last year Vale worked at a bakery for three months.
es: El año pasado Vale trabajó en una panadería durante tres meses.
why: Three months is a closed stretch.

en: I didn't know what to do and I kept looking at the door.
es: No sabía qué hacer y miraba la puerta.
why: Both are the state of mind at that moment, not finished events.

en: Suddenly I realized what to do, and I called Tomás.
es: De repente supe qué hacer y llamé a Tomás.
why: Suddenly marks the moment I found out.

en: Every morning Don Hernando read the newspaper before opening.
es: Cada mañana Don Hernando leía el periódico antes de abrir.
why: Every morning is a habit.

en: This morning Don Hernando read the whole newspaper in ten minutes.
es: Esta mañana Don Hernando leyó todo el periódico en diez minutos.
why: One finished reading, with a time given.

en: Tomás was tired and he was walking slowly.
es: Tomás estaba cansado y caminaba despacio.
why: Walking slowly is the scene, not an event.

en: Tomás was so tired that he fell asleep on the bus.
es: Tomás estaba tan cansado que se durmió en el bus.
why: Falling asleep is one event.

en: When Rosa was young, she sang at every party.
es: Cuando Rosa era joven, cantaba en todas las fiestas.
why: Every party means it used to happen.

en: Rosa sang one song and then went home.
es: Rosa cantó una canción y luego se fue a su casa.
why: Leaving is one event after the song.

en: Yesterday Vale arrived at six and opened the café.
es: Ayer Vale llegó a las seis y abrió el café.
why: One arrival, one day.

en: Vale arrived at six every day and opened the café.
es: Vale llegaba a las seis todos los días y abría el café.
why: Every day is a habit.

en: Rosa put the soup on the table and everyone started to eat.
es: Rosa puso la sopa en la mesa y todos empezaron a comer.
why: Putting the soup down is one event that starts the meal.

en: Tomás was waiting outside while it was getting dark.
es: Tomás esperaba afuera mientras oscurecía.
why: Two things going on at once, with no end in sight.

en: The power went out at nine and the whole street was dark.
es: A las nueve se fue la luz y toda la calle quedó a oscuras.
why: One event at a given time.

en: Hernando was a taxi driver, and he knew every street in Bogotá.
es: Hernando era taxista y conocía cada calle de Bogotá.
why: Knowing the streets is how things were.

en: Hernando met Rosa in 1980 and married her a year later.
es: Hernando conoció a Rosa en 1980 y se casó con ella un año después.
why: Meeting someone is one event.

en: Vale said yes and everyone clapped.
es: Vale dijo que sí y todos aplaudieron.
why: One answer, then a reaction.
